segs.text: Section eighteen. Drug target receptors. Drug targets are the third area of pharmacogenomics. They are less well characterized than metabolizing enzymes, and she gave only what she considers good science. A target variant can change how well a drug works, as with the beta one receptor and metoprolol. Or a target variant can cause the disease itself, so the drug is chosen because it hits that variant, as with E G F R and gefitinib.

The beta one receptor gene is A D R B one. Its non synonymous S N Ps are serine forty nine to glycine, and arginine three eighty nine to glycine. The variant changes the receptor, so metoprolol may not bind as well. Patients homozygous for serine forty nine and arginine three eighty nine, the wild type, had the better response, not the variant carriers. So a patient with the variants may respond poorly, and genotype may guide the choice of starting drug.

The beta two receptor gene is A D R B two, the target of beta two agonists such as albuterol. It has more than eleven S N Ps, and three are frequent, arginine sixteen to glycine, codon twenty seven, and the promoter. These are separate from the beta one S N Ps. Arginine sixteen to glycine is in beta two, not beta one.

At codon sixteen, A changes to G, so the codon A G A, for arginine, becomes G G A, for glycine. Arginine sixteen is called the wild type because it was identified first. The results for arginine sixteen to glycine are unclear. She said, This again, is not something that is likely to result in people being genotyped.

E G F R, also called H E R one or E R B B one, is the receptor for epidermal growth factor, which binds it and signals the cell to divide. In some non small cell lung cancers, a gain of function E G F R is overexpressed and drives division. Gefitinib binds the inside of the receptor and blocks the signal. Response was strongly tied to the mutation in two thousand four. Everyone has E G F R, but gefitinib works only when the tumor has the variant receptor, so it is used only then. She said, we're using this drug to assure efficacy, right? We're individualizing their care.

A very new area is the G proteins coupled to receptors. Variants, especially in the alpha subunit, are associated with the efficacy of some antidepressants. These variants sit in the G protein coupled to the receptor, not in the receptor itself. So a response that looks like it comes from the receptor may actually come from its G protein.
